correctness.rationale: For every alternating-parity quadruple of polygon vertices, both noncrossing completions are explicitly constructed by pairing consecutive vertices in the four intervening arcs. Their difference is one integral 2-by-2 checkerboard. For any fixed pair of even rows, realizable checkerboards connect every inside-arc odd column to every outside-arc odd column; this complete bipartite column graph is connected, so all checkerboards for those rows are integer sums. All standard zero-row/zero-column integer basis vectors are therefore generated. Real orthogonal complementation gives the exact covariance nullspace of row-plus-column potentials and rank (n-1)^2. Catalan one-edge and two-edge moment formulas follow from splitting the polygon into independent even-vertex faces. The embedded Python standard-library checker reproduced 8771 exact integer moment entries, 714 geometric flip witnesses, and all seven finite incidence ranks for n=2,...,8. Universal statements are proved algebraically, not inferred from finite checks.

Neither those statements nor the closest semantic research records inspected assert that the strictly smaller noncrossing matching set generates the entire integral zero-marginal lattice, or that anchored differences have maximal rank in every field. The original 2002 geometric matching article could not be inspected in full; an equivalent historical consequence remains a real residual risk and is explicitly recorded.

value.rationale: Noncrossing planar matchings sample only C_n of the n! possible bipartite assignments, so a natural structural question is whether forbidding crossings introduces additional first-order Fourier dependencies or arithmetic sampling obstructions. The theorem rules out both: row/column potentials are exactly the nullspace, every integer balanced perturbation is an integer combination of permitted sample differences, and maximal anchored rank persists over every field. This full arithmetic and probabilistic identifiability statement is a motivated classification for infinitely many polygon sizes, not an isolated Catalan-number recomputation. No quantitative stability constants are claimed.
